algorithm:vector_similarity.notes: Cosine in IR is usually credited to Salton's vector space model (SMART, 1975); we only read IIR Sec. 6.3.1 (secondary), not the 1975 paper, so the origin is a candidate. algorithm:embeddings.name: Embeddings and the embedding space

also_cite.why: The token encoder f_theta whose outputs h_i are pooled.

algorithm:embeddings.notes: The 'text to a point in space' idea has no single origin (word2vec 2013 for words, SBERT 2019 for pooled sentence vectors compared by cosine); we cite SBERT because the formula shown (mean pooling then cosine) is its default. algorithm:tfidf.name: TF-IDF

also_cite.why: Systematises tf x idf weighting variants (not opened).

also_cite.title: Introduction to Information Retrieval
also_cite.why: Textbook treatment of cosine (Sec. 6.3.1), tf-idf (Sec. 6.2).

algorithm:tfidf.notes: Spärck Jones 1972 read (2004 reprint) in an earlier session per the item's note; her weight is not the ln(N/n) form shown, which is the textbook form (IIR Eq. 6.7-6.9). tf x idf as a product is credited to Salton's group, Salton & Buckley 1988 not opened.

algorithm:bm25.name_fa: BM25 (اشباع k1 و نرمال‌سازی طول b)

introduced_by.title: Some Simple Effective Approximations to the 2-Poisson Model for Probabilistic Weighted Retrieval
introduced_by.why: Candidate origin of the saturating tf component and document-length normalisation that BM25 uses (not opened; paywalled). The BM25 name and exact weight appear in Okapi at TREC-3 (1994, NIST SP 500-225, no DOI).

also_cite.title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
also_cite.venue: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval 3(4):333-389

also_cite.title: Okapi at TREC-3
also_cite.why: First use of the name BM25 (candidate; not opened).

algorithm:bm25.notes: Origin papers not opened; the formula we show is the Lucene/Elasticsearch variant (IDF with +1), which is not printed in any of these papers. Keep the item status low until Robertson & Walker 1994 is read.

introduced_by.why: Defines RRFscore(d)=sum 1/(k+r(d)) with k=60 fixed in a pilot study (p.758-759).

algorithm:rrf_fusion.notes: Two-page paper; k=60 is near-optimal, not the maximum (Table 1, k=80 slightly higher), the paper says the choice was not critical.

algorithm:convex_fusion.notes: Linear score combination in IR is older (CombSUM, Fox & Shaw 1994; Vogt & Cottrell 1999; unverified, not looked up); Bruch et al. is the origin of the hybrid dense+sparse analysis and the names shown. Item's own note says the paper was read in the arXiv PDF.

introduced_by.why: Defines Maximal Marginal Relevance (the lambda-weighted argmax formula), p.335.

introduced_by.why: Introduces HNSW: exponentially decaying layer assignment l=floor(-ln(U) m_L), m_L=1/ln M, Algorithm 1.

algorithm:hnsw.notes: arXiv preprint appeared 2016 (OpenAlex arXiv record: 182 citations, separate from the 1850 of the TPAMI record). The NSW graph precursor is Malkov et al. 2014 (not looked up).

also_cite.why: Origin of the inverted-file over a clustered (visual-word) vocabulary that IVF generalises (candidate; not opened).

algorithm:ivf_pq.notes: Product quantization is credited here; the 'IVF' coarse quantizer idea predates it (Sivic & Zisserman), status of that link is unverified. OpenAlex lists the paper as 2010 (online) vs 2011 issue.

algorithm:chunking.name: Chunking (size, overlap, structure)

introduced_by.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
introduced_by.why: Sec. 4.1: splits each Wikipedia article into disjoint 100-word passages (the fixed-size chunking used as the retrieval unit); gives no chunk-count or storage formula.

also_cite.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
also_cite.why: Sec. 3: each Wikipedia article split into disjoint 100-word chunks (21M documents) as the retrieval index.

also_cite.title: Reconstructing Context: Evaluating Advanced Chunking Strategies for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
also_cite.why: Compares late chunking and contextual retrieval against fixed chunking; abstract and introduction checked.

algorithm:chunking.notes: Fixed-size disjoint 100-word passages are evidenced as common practice in DPR (Sec. 4.1) and RAG (Sec. 3), neither of which invented chunking. Our chunk-count, storage and cut-probability formulas are our own arithmetic with no origin paper.

algorithm:entity_linking.name: GraphRAG: entity linking

introduced_by.title: Scalable Zero-shot Entity Linking with Dense Entity Retrieval
introduced_by.why: Introduces BLINK: a bi-encoder that embeds mention context and entity text independently for dense retrieval (dot-product score), then a cross-encoder re-ranks candidates.

also_cite.title: Neural Entity Linking: A Survey of Models Based on Deep Learning
also_cite.why: Survey: splits entity linking into mention detection and entity disambiguation (introduction).

algorithm:entity_linking.notes: Dense bi-encoder entity linking is BLINK; entity linking as a task is older (not traced). The use of linking to pick graph start nodes in GraphRAG is our synthesis. Semantic Scholar merges arXiv versions (182); OpenAlex arXiv record shows 20.

algorithm:k_hop.name: GraphRAG: k-hop / BFS expansion

introduced_by.title: Understanding Graph Embedding Methods and Their Applications
introduced_by.why: Sec. 2.2.2: defines the k-hop neighborhood as vertices reachable in k hops or fewer; a survey, not the first definition.

also_cite.title: Introduction to Algorithms (4th ed.), chapter Elementary Graph Algorithms (breadth-first search)
also_cite.why: Textbook treatment of breadth-first search, which computes shortest hop distances ring by ring (chapter number not re-opened; ISBN not re-checked against the user's copy).

also_cite.title: The shortest path through a maze
also_cite.venue: Proc. Int. Symposium on the Theory of Switching, Harvard Univ. Press, pp. 285-292
also_cite.why: Usually credited as the first published description of breadth-first search as a shortest-path method (not located online or read here).

algorithm:k_hop.notes: k-hop neighborhood and breadth-first search are standard graph theory with no single origin paper; Moore 1959 is the usual BFS credit (not read). Xu 2021 (SIAM Review) is a survey that states the definition; PDF is in the user's Zotero (AQMNUKM6), not downloaded here.

algorithm:personalized_pagerank.name: GraphRAG: Personalized PageRank (HippoRAG)

introduced_by.title: Topic-Sensitive PageRank
introduced_by.why: Sec. 2: PageRank computed with a non-uniform personalization (bias) vector; Eq. 5 Rank = (1-alpha) M Rank + alpha p. The paper says the idea of biasing PageRank was suggested earlier (Page et al.).

also_cite.title: The PageRank Citation Ranking: Bringing Order to the Web
also_cite.why: Original PageRank; mentions a personalization/teleport vector. Not opened here (Stanford server returned HTTP 500 on 2026-10-08/09).

also_cite.title: Scaling personalized web search
also_cite.why: Defines personalized PageRank (PPR) over a preference set and gives a way to compute it at scale. Not opened (PDF not obtained).

also_cite.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
also_cite.why: Sec. 2.2/3.4: runs Personalized PageRank over the KG with the query's entities as seeds (restart probability 0.5) to retrieve passages.

algorithm:personalized_pagerank.notes: Personalization of PageRank was suggested by Page et al. 1999 and formalised by Jeh & Widom 2003 and Haveliwala 2002; Haveliwala's Eq. 5 is the one we checked. Page and Jeh-Widom were not opened. HippoRAG (2024) applies PPR to retrieval; it did not invent PPR.

algorithm:leiden_communities.name: GraphRAG: community detection (Leiden) and modularity

introduced_by.title: From Louvain to Leiden: guaranteeing well-connected communities
introduced_by.why: Introduces the Leiden algorithm; abstract: Louvain yields up to 25% badly connected and 16% disconnected communities, Leiden guarantees connected communities; modularity with resolution parameter gamma (Eq. 1).

also_cite.title: Finding and evaluating community structure in networks
also_cite.why: Introduces the modularity measure Q for scoring a partition of a network into communities (Sec. on modularity).

also_cite.title: Fast unfolding of communities in large networks
also_cite.why: Introduces the Louvain heuristic (modularity optimization by local moving and aggregation), which Leiden improves.

algorithm:leiden_communities.notes: Item has two parts: the Leiden algorithm (Traag 2019) and the modularity objective, which Newman & Girvan 2004 introduced (term 'modularity' located in their PDF); Louvain (Blondel 2008) is the predecessor. The resolution parameter gamma is from Reichardt & Bornholdt (2006), not looked up.

algorithm:ms_local_global.name: GraphRAG: Microsoft local vs global search (map-reduce)
algorithm:ms_local_global.name_fa: GraphRAG: جست‌وجوی محلی در برابر جست‌وجوی سراسری Microsoft (نگاشت‌کاهش)

introduced_by.why: Sec. 3.1.6: global search as map-reduce over Leiden community summaries (helpfulness score 0-100, filter score 0, sort and fill the context window); local search is documented in the GraphRAG docs.

algorithm:ms_local_global.notes: Global search (map-reduce over community summaries) is in the paper; local search is described only in the GraphRAG documentation (microsoft.github.io/graphrag), which changes with releases. The call-count formula is ours.

algorithm:pcst_gretriever.name: GraphRAG: G-Retriever PCST subgraph

introduced_by.title: G-Retriever: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Textual Graph Understanding and Question Answering
introduced_by.why: Formulates subgraph retrieval for RAG as a Prize-Collecting Steiner Tree problem (prize Eq. 6, objective Eq. 7, cost Eq. 8).

also_cite.title: A General Approximation Technique for Constrained Forest Problems
also_cite.why: Standard reference for a 2-approximation of the prize-collecting Steiner tree problem; not opened here (paywalled), so its exact scope is unverified. The PCST problem itself is older (Bienstock et al. 1993, not looked up).

algorithm:pcst_gretriever.notes: G-Retriever introduced PCST for RAG subgraph retrieval; the PCST optimisation problem is classical (Goemans & Williamson 1995 give an approximation; paywalled, not opened).

algorithm:lightrag_dual.name: GraphRAG: LightRAG dual-level retrieval

introduced_by.title: LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation
introduced_by.why: Section on dual-level retrieval: low-level (entity) and high-level (theme) keywords matched to entities and relations in a vector store, plus one-hop neighbours.

algorithm:lightrag_dual.notes: Dual-level retrieval is defined in LightRAG; cosine ranking, k=1 and the toy vectors are our choices.

algorithm:path_scoring.name: GraphRAG: path scoring

introduced_by.title: PathRAG: Pruning Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation with Relational Paths
introduced_by.why: Section 'Path Retrieval': flow-based pruning with resource propagation (Eq. 2), early stopping (Eq. 3) and path reliability score (Eq. 4); alpha=0.7, N=40, K=15.

algorithm:path_scoring.notes: PathRAG is the closest primary source for scoring paths as evidence; other path-ranking methods exist and were not compared. Citation count is low because the paper is recent.

algorithm:graph_vector_combination.name: GraphRAG: combining graph and vector scores
algorithm:graph_vector_combination.name_fa: GraphRAG: ترکیب امتیازهای گراف و بردار

also_cite.why: Analyses convex-combination score fusion of lexical and semantic retrieval; basis for our weighted-sum form.

algorithm:graph_vector_combination.notes: HybridRAG combines graph and vector context by ordered concatenation, not a weighted sum; the weighted sum with 1/(1+hops) is our engineering construction, after convex fusion in Bruch et al. 2023 (a different setting: lexical + dense scores). No origin paper for the exact formula.

introduced_by.why: Sec. 3.5: semantic cache = embed the query, retrieve Top-K cached queries, a similarity evaluator decides a hit; no threshold equation or cost formula.

algorithm:semantic_cache.notes: GPTCache describes the semantic-cache pattern (embed, Top-K lookup, similarity evaluator) but gives no threshold or cost formula; the rule max cos >= tau and the cost arithmetic are ours (a common configurable option in the GPTCache code).

also_cite.why: Provider documentation: automatic prefix reuse, 1,024-token minimum. Not re-opened here.

algorithm:kv_prompt_cache.notes: Reuse of KV states across prompts: Prompt Cache (Nov 2023) states the idea for modular prompts; vLLM (Sep 2023, block sharing) and SGLang RadixAttention (prefix tree) are parallel work, so priority among them is not settled here. Provider price multipliers come from docs, not papers. Cost formula is ours.

introduced_by.why: Candidate origin of the trace/span model of distributed tracing that OpenTelemetry and MLflow Tracing build on; not read here.

also_cite.why: Documentation of span attributes (gen_ai.*) and trace capture; status Development; opened 2026-10-08 by an earlier check, not re-opened.

component:guard.name: Input guardrail

also_cite.title: Llama Guard: LLM-based Input-Output Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations
also_cite.why: An LLM that classifies prompts (input) and responses (output) against a safety taxonomy (abstract).

also_cite.title: Ignore Previous Prompt: Attack Techniques For Language Models
also_cite.why: Defines prompt injection as inserting malicious text to misalign an LLM (Sec. 1); the attack that an input guardrail must catch.

component:qcache.name: Cache check

introduced_by.title: GPTCache: An Open-Source Semantic Cache for LLM Applications Enabling Faster Answers and Cost Savings
introduced_by.why: Semantic cache for LLM calls: the query is embedded, a vector store is searched for a similar earlier query, and the stored response is returned (abstract; arXiv-less ACL workshop paper).

component:qcache.notes: Semantic cache of LLM answers by embedding similarity is GPTCache (Zilliz tool paper). Exact-match response caching is older and has no origin paper; this is the earliest published semantic-cache paper I found, not proven earliest.

component:route.name: Routing

introduced_by.title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
introduced_by.why: A small classifier LM predicts query complexity and routes to no retrieval, single-step or multi-step RAG (abstract, Fig. 2).

also_cite.title: LangChain, RAG From Scratch (routing: logical and semantic)
also_cite.why: Source of the logical/semantic routing wording on the page; vendor repo, not an origin paper.

component:route.notes: Adaptive-RAG routes by query complexity (retrieval strategy), a related but different routing from the page's data-source and prompt routing. No origin paper found for logical/semantic routing, which is a LangChain pattern; Adaptive-RAG is a candidate only.

component:rerank.name: Rerank + refine

introduced_by.title: Passage Re-ranking with BERT
introduced_by.why: Feeds query and passage jointly ([CLS] q [SEP] p) to BERT and re-ranks candidates by the classifier probability; state of the art on TREC-CAR and MS MARCO (abstract).

also_cite.title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
also_cite.why: A lightweight retrieval evaluator grades retrieved documents (correct / incorrect / ambiguous), triggers web search, and a decompose-then-recompose step filters the text (abstract).

also_cite.title: Introducing Contextual Retrieval
also_cite.why: Vendor documentation, not a paper: LLM-written context per chunk, BM25 + embeddings, reranking; failure rate 5.7% to 1.9%. Not an origin paper.

component:rerank.notes: Record reused from algorithm:cross_encoder. Reranking with a stronger model: Nogueira & Cho 2019 for BERT re-ranking. The refinement half (drop or correct weak results, re-retrieve) is CRAG (Yan et al. 2024, abstract read).

component:augment.name: Augment

introduced_by.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
introduced_by.why: Sec. 2 (BART generator): the retrieved passage z is concatenated with the input x before the generator (read in the PDF); this is the prompt-augmentation step.

also_cite.title: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
also_cite.why: Prepends the retrieved document to the input of an unchanged LM, with no further training (abstract, Fig. 2).

component:augment.notes: In-Context RALM (Ram et al. 2023) is the decoder-only, no-training version that prepends documents to the prompt, which is what the page's Augment box draws. Source-id citation and prompt layout are engineering choices with no origin paper.

component:generate.name: Generate

introduced_by.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
introduced_by.why: Sec. 2: a seq2seq generator (BART) produces the output conditioned on input and retrieved passages; retriever and generator trained end to end.

also_cite.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
also_cite.why: Trains one LM that retrieves on demand and critiques passages and its own output with reflection tokens (abstract, Sec. 1).

component:generate.notes: Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2024) supplies the active-retrieval variant (retrieve on demand, critique with reflection tokens); abstract and Sec. 1 read. Citing chunk ids in the answer is covered by ALCE (Gao et al. 2023), see metric chunks.

component:cache.name: Caching
